summary: An Indologist, Christopher Minkowski studied at Harvard, Delhi, and under Daniel H. H. Ingalls. He held posts at Oxford, including Boden Professor of Sanskrit (2005–2023), and served as Professor at Cornell University (1989–2006).

Working in Indology and history and archaeology, Christopher Pinney became professor of anthropology and visual culture at University College London around 2000. He also held posts at Chicago, Northwestern, Cape Town, Jawaharlal Nehru University, and Australian National University.

Working in Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and Indology, Christopher S. George studied at Columbia under Royal W. Weiler, Geshe Wangyal, and Pema Gyaltsen. He founded the American Institute of Buddhist Studies and was a professor at IASWR.

Christopher S. Queen worked in Buddhist and religious studies at Harvard University, serving as Dean of Students for Continuing Education and lecturer on Religion (~1989–2008), and later as Lecturer on Buddhism and World Religions.

Christopher Wallis, an Indologist and religious studies scholar, studied at Rochester, Oxford under Alexis Sanderson, and UC Berkeley under Robert P. Goldman and Alexander von Rospatt. He was a guest lecturer at Naropa University in 2020.

Chu-tsing Li worked in sinology and history/archaeology, studying at the University of Nanking and the University of Iowa. He taught English at Nanking (1943–1947), was an art history professor at Iowa (~1956–1966), and joined Kansas in 1966.
A Buddhist studies scholar, Chuichi Kimura held academic posts at Minobusan University, where he is attested as an associate professor in 2015 and as a former professor in 2026.

A philosopher and sinologist, Chun-i Tang studied at National Central University and under Shili Xiong and Thomé H. Fang. He was a professor at Central University, New Asia Institute, and first Chair Professor at CUHK (1963–1974).

Working in Buddhist studies and sinology, Chun-min Yen earned a PhD from the University of Arizona, studying under Robert M. Gimello and Todd Brown, and received traditional training under Chanyun and Sheng Yen.
Chung-pui Tai is a scholar of linguistics, sinology, and Tibetology who studied at the Graduate School of the Chinese Academy of Social Sciences and held a post at the University of Hong Kong.

A Buddhist studies and Tibetology scholar, Chögyam Trungpa studied at Oxford and with teachers including Khenpo Gangshar. He served at the Young Lamas Home School (1959–1963) and founded Naropa University, Samye Ling Monastery, and Shambhala International.

Chökyi Gyatso studied under Jamgon Ju Mipham Gyatso, Jamgön Kongtrül Lodrö Thaye, Khakyab Dorje, and Jamyang Khyentse Chökyi Lodrö, and taught Jamyang Khyentse Chökyi Lodrö and Khunu Lama Tenzin Gyaltsen.
Chökyi Nyima studied under Jamyang Khyentse Chökyi Lodrö and Dudjom Rinpoche.

Active in Buddhist studies and Tibetology, Chökyi Nyima Rinpoche studied at Rumtek Monastery under the 16th Karmapa and Dilgo Khyentse. He founded the Rangjung Yeshe Institute, served as abbot of Ka-Nying Shedrub Ling, and presided over DCT.
Chökyi Nyinche studied under Jamgön Kongtrül Lodrö Thaye and Shechen Gyaltsab, and taught Dilgo Khyentse Rinpoche.
Chönyi Drolma is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Tibetology who studied under Thinley Norbu Rinpoche, Lama Tharchin Rinpoche, and Ngawang Zangpo.
Chüan-ying Yen is a scholar in Buddhist studies, sinology, and history/archaeology. She earned her PhD at Harvard University, studying under John M. Rosenfield, Chu-tsing Li, and John Hay.

Chün-fang Yü is a scholar of Buddhist studies, sinology, and religious studies. She studied at Columbia University, taught at Rutgers University (~1972–2001), and served as Professor and Sheng Yen Professor Emerita at Columbia.

A historian, Clara Sue Kidwell earned her PhD at the University of Oklahoma. She held posts at UC Berkeley, the National Museum of the American Indian, Oklahoma as Native American studies director, and UNC Chapel Hill as director.

A scholar of philosophy and religious studies, Clare Carlisle studied at Trinity College, Cambridge (1995–2002). She was a Lecturer in Philosophy at the University of Liverpool (~2006–2011) and became a professor at King's College London around 2011.
